events.title: William the Conqueror Lands at Pevensey
events.description: William, Duke of Normandy, landed with his invasion force at Pevensey on the south coast of England, beginning his campaign to claim the English throne. This came just days after Harold Godwinson defeated Norwegian forces at Stamford Bridge.
events.significance: The landing led to the Battle of Hastings in October 1066 and the Norman conquest of England, which transformed English language, law, nobility, and culture.

events.title: U.S. Army Established by Congress
events.description: The First United States Congress passed an act creating a regular army of about 700 men, continuing the force that had been maintained under the Articles of Confederation.
events.significance: It marked the formal establishment of a permanent national military force under the new Constitution, forming the foundation of the modern U.S. Army.

events.title: Metropolitan Police Founded in London
events.description: Home Secretary Robert Peel's Metropolitan Police Force, whose officers became known as 'Bobbies' or 'Peelers', began operating in London, with officers first appearing on the streets.
events.significance: It is regarded as the model for modern civilian policing, emphasizing crime prevention and public consent, and influenced police forces worldwide.

events.title: Death of Émile Zola
events.description: The French novelist and journalist Émile Zola died in Paris from carbon monoxide poisoning caused by a blocked chimney. He was the leading figure of the naturalist literary movement and author of the Rougon-Macquart novel cycle.
events.significance: Zola's open letter 'J'Accuse...!' defended Alfred Dreyfus and became a landmark in the fight against injustice and antisemitism, shaping the role of public intellectuals.

events.title: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn Citizenship Restored
events.description: The Soviet government under Mikhail Gorbachev moved toward restoring citizenship to exiled writer Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, and his work The Gulag Archipelago was soon to be published in the USSR as Soviet censorship collapsed.
events.significance: It symbolized the thaw of Soviet repression and the reckoning with the Stalinist past in the final years of the Soviet Union.
